utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Case number IT-04-74- T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic and others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I'd like to greet the Prosecution, the witness, the Defence teams, the accused. I note that Mr. Pusic is still not amongst us. The registrar should find out exactly what is wrong with him by contacting the relevant authorities. Is he seriously ill? Mr. Ibrisimovic, do you have any information about the state your client is?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, yesterday I was told he had a temperature and a bad cold. I don't know what the situation is today, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope he will recover very rapidly so that he can attend the hearings. I believe Mr. Kovacic wanted to take the floor with regard to an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if this is an appropriate time I'd like to deal with this. It's Exhibit 3D 00278, on the 29th of August, the Defence tendered this. It was the conclusion from the Ministry of Defence of Croatia, 15th of June 1993 and they said that active military service for Mr. Slobodan Praljak should be terminated. That was with regard to Witness BJ. The Chamber then asked the Defence to provide other rules referred to in the introduction to that conclusion, that decision, from the ministry dated the 15th of June. 5712 is the page in the transcript, 18 to 25, lines 18 to 25. As you have requested, we carried out this additional work and 3D 00278 was marked for identification. We then took those rules referred to in the introduction to the decision, we had them translated, and they are now in the e-court system under number 3D 00372. That's one of the laws. And 3D 00373. That's another law. They are now in the e-court system and we therefore suggest that these two new documents, 372 and 373 now be admitted into evidence in relation to the first exhibit, 00278, and we can now have 3D 00278 definitively admitted into evidence. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We'll examine these three documents and we will hand down a decision. We'll now continue with the hearing, protective measures must be in place since we have the screen there. Mr. Mundis, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel and to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. President, while proofing this witness yesterday morning, he indicated a preference for or the need for protective measures in the form of facial distortion only, as will be clear in a few moments, this witness was the victim of among other things sexual assault, the Prosecution alleges, and the witness has indicated although he has no objection to his statement being made public, nor to his identity being made public, so as to avoid being recognised on the street in his community, he would prefer that facial distortion be afforded as a protective measure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We have understood the reasons for this request. I'll confer with my colleagues. The Chamber grants the request. Mr. Registrar, take the steps necessary for visual distortion, please. Sir, could you please stand up? Could you tell me your name, and profession and your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Ragib Mulahusic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 2nd of January 1955.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Place of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the municipality of Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, have you already testified before national or International Tribunal with regard to the events that took place in your country? Or is this the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please read out the text that the usher will show you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, please sit down. Sir, I'd like to provide you with some information. This is a new procedure we will be following. The Prosecution will be asking you whether you gave a statement to the OTP. Then the Prosecution will show you some documents to you and ask whether you can recognise them. Once this has been done, the Defence who are to your left and who represent the accused, will conduct the cross-examination and put questions to you that concern your written statements. Three judges before you usually there are four of us but one of the Judges is absent pursuant to 15 bis of the Rules of Procedure, but the Judges sitting before you may put questions to you at any point in time. When the Judges do so, it's because pursuant to 90(F) of the rules, the Judges try to put useful questions to witnesses for the sake of truth. Sometimes the objection might have objections when Defence questions you, the Chamber will see whether the questions can then be authorised. As a rule, the Judges are in favour of an adversarial principle followed when questions are put and it is only exceptionally that we recognise certain objections. Our purpose is to determine what actually happened so naturally we are in favour of everything that a witness can tell us. That's what I wanted to inform you of. And now without wasting any more time I will give the floor to the Prosecution so that they can follow this new procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. For the benefit of the public, the Prosecution is prepared to provide a brief oral summary of the written testimony of this witness, if that would be helpful. This is taken, Mr. President, and Your Honours, directly from the Rule 65 ter summary. On 1 August 1993, the witness, a Muslim male, was arrested in a house in Prozor and taken to the secondary school in Prozor town. From that school, he was taken to work for the Croatian Defence Council, the HVO, as a butcher at one of the butcher shops in Prozor and he was also taken out of the school to perform forced labour. On one occasion, he was brought with 21 other prisoners to the village of Jurici, where he was detained and from where they were taken to dig trenches. After being detained in Jurici for a few days, HVO soldiers told the witness and others to take off their clothing and the detainees were forced to perform oral sex on each other. After approximately 25 days in Jurici, the prisoners were taken back to the secondary school in Prozor during which time, during the course of the detention there, the witness and others were beaten by HVO Soldiers. The witness was subsequently transferred to the Heliodrom and was released from the Heliodrom on 18 April 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.A. Good afternoon.Q. Sir, did you ever provide a written statement to investigators of theOffice of the Prosecutor of the ICTY?A. Yes.Q. Do you recall, sir, approximately when you gave this statement?A. It says when in the statement, the 10th of January, 2001. The 10th was the date.Q. Sir, I suggest to you that it was actually the 10th of April 2001.Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, at the time you provided this written statement, did you answer the questions of the investigator truthfully?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I said I spoke the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, did you answer the questions freely, that is without any coercion?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Freely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And at the conclusion of that interview, sir, was your statement read back to you in the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, in the Bosnian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, did you then sign that statement in the English language?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes -- no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you, sir, which version of your statement do you remember signing, the English version or the Bosnian version?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I think it was the Bosnian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. With the assistance of the usher, Mr. President, I have English and Bosnian language copies of the statement and I would ask that these be provided to the witness. Perhaps they can be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Mulahusic, you have before you now both the English and Bosnian versions of your statement. Can you tell us which version or versions of that statement you actually signed in 2001?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, my signature is here. My signatures are here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And your signature, sir, is on the English version; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you travelled, Mr. Mulahusic, here to The Hague a few days ago, you met with an investigator and myself yesterday. You recall that?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And at that point in time, were you given the opportunity to review your statement in the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, could we just check if the ELMO is working? We don't seem to be able to see the statement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need to see the signature. There, we have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm also informed, Mr. President, for the benefit of everyone that these two statements are in e-court as P 09699, in both English and Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Mulahusic, yesterday, upon reviewing your statement in the Bosnian language, did you have any -- did you have any corrections to make to that statement?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you have any additions to that statement, having had the opportunity to review it in the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Having had the opportunity to review the statement in the Bosnian language, was there anything that you wanted to delete from your April 2001 written statement?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No, there was nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Mulahusic, if I were to ask you questions about the subject matters contained in your written statement, would the answers reflect what's written in that statement of April 2001?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And there is nothing that you would like to add to that statement?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Mr. President, Your Honours, the Prosecution would tender P 09699, the written statement of Mr. Mulahusic dated 10 April 2001, into evidence. We have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Mr. Mundis. I believe initially you had planned to use up one hour. The Defence has an hour. It's for you to use the time as you see fit. If you haven't agreed on how to divide the time you'll have ten minutes each. If you have reached an agreement, well, it's as you wish to proceed. I'll give the floor to the first Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, Mr. Coric's Defence has no questions for this witness, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And the next Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MR. MULALIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Prlic's Defence has no questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Our Defence has no questions, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Praljak's Defence has a few questions for this witness. Cross-examination by Mr. Kovacic

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good day, I represent General Praljak here. Naturally we have read through your statement. It was summarised here today and I'll just put a few questions to you so that we can clarify a few issues. And since we speak the same language, and what we say is being interpreted, I'd be grateful if you could pause briefly after I put my question to you and then answer the question. First of all, in your statement, you said how you had been arrested and when and you said you were arrested on the 1st of August 1993 in your house in Prozor and you were taken to the school. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us who arrested you?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, it was the HVO but I didn't know them. The insignia they had was HVO insignia. They were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So they were wearing uniforms, camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, uniforms, camouflage uniforms, HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So they had HVO insignia?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you see the insignia?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you see any additional kinds of insignia that indicated which HVO units they were part of?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No. I only saw that it said HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And then you were taken to the school?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Is it true that there were two guards in front of the entrance to the school at all times?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Two or three. I was up on the floor. I didn't have the opportunity of counting them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Very well. And these guards, were they also wearing camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was the HVO, the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did they have HVO insignia? Did the police have HVO insignia?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's now go back to the year 1992, early 1992. And from the beginning of 1992, did you go to the front lines to defend Bosnia- Herzegovina against the Serbian aggression and the JNA aggression?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Does that mean that you weren't mobilised as part of the defence?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I was mobilised as a worker. I worked as a butcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, you weren't mobilised -- just a minute, because of the interpretation. I'll assist. Given what you have said, you can confirm whether that's correct or not. You were mobilised but you were mobilised into civilian units, not into combat units?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you perform those civilian duties for which you had been mobilised?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You did?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I introduce a very small question? When you were mobilised and worked as a butcher did you also wear some kind of a uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ordinary clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And to follow up, other individuals who were mobilised into civilian service were wearing ordinary clothes? [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us how this was organised? Did you sometimes -- were you sometimes asked to go to a certain place, certain time, carry out certain work?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: A person came to get me, a person came to get me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And other individuals too?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Very well. And you would work during the day and go home at night is that how it worked?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So you performed civilian duties, it was called a work obligation at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. After they had arrested you, you said that you were taken to the school, you were there with other people who were in the same situation that you were in and a few brief questions: We can see from your statement and other statements that you slept in the class rooms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: They gave you some kind of mattresses and blankets there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Depended. Not everyone. Everyone had a mattress. Only some people had blankets.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could one say that most people had mattresses and blankets?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did the situation improve with time, as far as the mattresses and blankets are concerned? Did everyone get them or not?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you provided with food?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you notice whether you received the same kind of food as the soldiers who were there?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You don't know or you didn't notice then?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I didn't notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Was it allowed for families to take food to you?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: In the school, yes. Most of them were allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So if a family wanted to take food to you, you could receive that food?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Very well. Were you provided with medical care? Could you ask for a doctor's assistance, for a checkup?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, sometimes, yes. Not everyone could, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did doctors go to see you when you were there?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Once a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you agree that it was at least ones a week and when necessary, if someone requested a doctor's assistance, it happened more frequently?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And then you worked in Prozor at a butcher's. Was that also treated as a work obligation?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You were told that you were continuing with your work obligation?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us which butcher you worked for, given us his name?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Pao, now, whether his surname was Maric, I don't know, but he worked for the cooperative.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Fine. And that butcher's shop supplied the army and civilians with meat, with food?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: The army, the HVO, but the HVO, but the Armija was there as well afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Whether you say the Armija, you mean the BH army?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, the BH army was there for a time and later on, just the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But that butcher's shop supplied all those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Who was the chief? Who was your boss, your immediate boss in the butcher shop?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: That man Pao [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Was his conduct proper towards you?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could you go home if you needed to do something, have a wash or something like that?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Is it true, as far as I can understand, that you have no complaints of your treatment while you worked in the butcher shop?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, his conduct was proper towards me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. After sometime passed, you were included in this group with some of our other colleagues and you were taken off to Jurici?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you spent about 25 days in all in Jurici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm not going to go into detail now but you described the incidents when you were abused and your other friends were abused, your fellow citizens. Is it true that those incidents which you spoke about and there were several, there were a number of them, is it true and correct that they took place mostly at night?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, mostly at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you describe when you say mostly at night, all five incidents, did only one of these take place during the night or four or --

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Do you mean soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, I mean these incidents?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, it lasted 10 or 11 hours and then until 2.00 or 3.00 a.m., 2 or 3 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It was always at night?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well for five or six days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You mean five or six times?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Five or six nights.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you perhaps know or had occasion to see when you were in Jurici who was the commander of that sector there where you were with the other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I wasn't interested in that at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I don't mean his name but did you notice that there was a person in uniform who acted as a commander, who was the commander there?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, everybody did what they wanted. I can't say. I can't say this one or that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So does that mean that it didn't really resemble an army if they didn't have a commander?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know who the commander was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Nobody imposed themselves and through their conduct and behaviour and issued orders go here, go there, that you came to the conclusion that that person was in command of those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Right, you weren't. Now, this abuse that took place --

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: -- apart from the abuse at night, during the night, can you tell us whether it happened during the day on just one occasion or perhaps two occasions or never?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, when this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I put this clear? You have first said it was or you have answered positively to the question did this happen during the night. But then you have also said that it usually lasted 10 to 12 hours, I think, and it ended at 2.00 in the morning. So one must assume that it started during the afternoon, that is before night. Have I understood you correctly or have I misunderstood you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. From 10 or 11.00 in the evening, 10 or 11 p.m., 10 or 11 p.m. is what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you could see that in the Croatian but perhaps not in the interpretation, but thank you for clearing that up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: On those occasions when you said there was abuse that took place during the day as well, on those occasions, you mentioned certain individuals and also you mentioned some names related to those incidents at night, and I'll mention some of their names. You mentioned a person called Goran, then there was Jozo, then Pesa?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you described some of them. You said that Goran was about 25 years old, that Jozo was about 30, that Pesa was about 40?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All this abuse that took place, was it always done by the people you mentioned or were more people involved in the abuse?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well mostly them but others too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So there were others too?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we say that these three or four men were the leaders, if I can put it that way, the ring leaders?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if they were the ring leaders but they would come in first and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you notice any additional insignia on those people except the HVO which denoted that they belonged to some other formation?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Among those people, did you recognise some locals from Rama perhaps or were they people who had come in from elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, Prozor is a large place. I don't know. I wasn't actually there for me to be able to recognise people much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: There were 25 of you there?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm sure you talked amongst yourselves?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did somebody else say he knew those people from Rama or did you think that they had come in from elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I just knew those three men and their names. I knew how they were called, what they were called.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Fine. But you learnt their names up there, you didn't know their names from before?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Mulahusic, for those answers. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just as a follow-up question from the Bench, you said that there were three and you gave us their names. You said Goran, Pesa and Jozo. Now, in your written statement, with respect to the man named Goran, you said that he was a member of the Croatian army. What does that mean exactly, to your mind? Was he a member of the HVO or was he a member of the Croatian army coming from Zagreb? What was your understanding? What did you mean to say when you used those words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the HVO. Now, whether it was the HVO army or -- I can't really say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Thank you. So you said the HVO. Now, when you were in Jurici, in your written statement, you said that you were doing work digging trenches. Am I right in understanding that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Da" you say; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you dug trenches the whole day, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the whole day. Whether it was raining or sunshine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Now, when you were digging trenches for the HVO, who was opposite the HVO on the opposite side? Were they the Serbs or was it the BH army, the army of Bosnia- Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The BH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And when you were digging the trenches from time to time, was there any shooting, any gunshots, across the BH army line or were you able to dig in peace, with no shooting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, they shot rarely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And when you were digging, did you have the feeling of being exposed to gunshots coming from the BH army line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, on rare occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And amongst your comrades, was anybody wounded to your knowledge, injured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I just noted on one occasion that Osman Pilav was wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The lines of the BH army, were at what distance from the trenches, 100 metres, 200 metres, 300 metres, one kilometre? How far away were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can't say exactly but it was far away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you returned to Prozor, to the school there, you said that you were beaten. Did that happen frequently that you were beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, five or six nights.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And who beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the people I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it was the same men who forced you to have oral sex also came at the secondary school -- to the secondary school and continued to beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they didn't beat us in the school. They beat us in Jurici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in your opinion, why were you beaten? Was there a reason of any kind? What was it due to? Why were you beaten, the blows that you received? Why did you receive them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can't know why they beat me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now my last question. It's a little anecdotic, perhaps, but it just came to my mind. We -- I would like to know the following: For a time, you were a butcher in Prozor, and then you went to that secondary school. Tell us why you didn't use the occasion to escape.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I didn't dare because of my family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise but you reminded me of something that I omitted to ask, just one question with the Court's indulgence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, when you were freed or even before, when you were taken to the Heliodrom, or when you were liberated in April 1994, did you tell -- report these atrocities to any of the authorities, the atrocities that happened to you?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You didn't go to any authority and write out a report or --

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No. I just gave this statement here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You mean to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But they called you and asked you about it and asked you to make a statement?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But you didn't go to -- when you were in the Heliodrom, did you ask for somebody to write down your statement about these abuses and atrocities in Jurici?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: At the Heliodrom, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you were released from Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I went to Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you report it to the Bosnian authorities when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you were called by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But you didn't go of your own accord and report what had happened?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The statement that you saw today?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You gave the statement when they called you up from the OTP and probably they were helped by the local police, they called you and asked you to make a statement about the events; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, my question is the following: Did you ever before go to any authority of your own free will and made a statement, gave a statement?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Going on from this, can you give us an explanation why you did not spontaneously make a complaint to authorities in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, how should I know? I can't really say, give you anything definite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Well, only you can know why you did or did not do something. I will try to assist you and put the question more directly. Was this something that you would regard as a shame? Could it be that you were ashamed of telling authorities about what had happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. I would then like to go to two other points that are raised in your statement. One is you say that an HVO soldier took a tooth out of Sejad Islamovic. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: This is surprising. Have you -- was there any reason given for this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, how should I know? I just saw it happen five or six metres away from where I was standing. I saw him take the tooth out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Had Mr. Islamovic complained of tooth ache?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the tooth, was it a golden tooth that he pulled out? Gold tooth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: The other incident I would like to return to is you say that Pesa shot above your head. Now, did he threaten you that he would kill you before you -- before he shot above your head?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He just stood me up against the wall and shot above my head. Then I heard five or six bullets, I fell down and didn't know what was happening, what happened after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Did you expect him to kill you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, how should I know what other people have in their heads?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Actually I was asking what you had in your head, your own head, at that time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I thought the worst.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Alaburic?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence of General Petkovic has no questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Coric?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I be allowed to ask two or three questions of this witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: Witness, I am the accused Valentin Coric.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you said that for a time, you were in the central military prison Heliodrom; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that you were guarded there by military personnel wearing a white belt with the HVO insignia on one shoulder and a military police insignia on the other shoulder and a big metal badge saying, military police, HVO? Do you remember those people, at least those white belts that they wore, that they were people who guarded you and provided security at the central prison in Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly not overlap?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: We don't have the answer yet.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was inside. I know that it was the police. Now, whether the HVO was there, I couldn't know -- I didn't know much about that but I worked in the kitchen for a time, towards the last period.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's precisely why I'm asking you this. What was these people's behaviour towards you regardless of how they were dressed in the Heliodrom? You weren't abused?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I can't say that I was when I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'm asking you all this because you said that when you were in the secondary school centre in Rama, that you were guarded by the police. Do you remember --

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what insignia the police had?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: They had belts.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: They had white belts?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because another witness who was here said that there were some other people there. Was it always the police or did they change?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you in detail because I went to Jurici from time to time. I would leave from time to time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: And in Jurici were you guarded by the police?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, when were you in the secondary school centre, these policemen, did they abuse you?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: This depended on the people. Some yes, some know. to escape.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't dare because of my family.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: What about you personally?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: Did you see any -- anybody else being mistreated before your very eyes?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: They would be taken down to the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: Yes. But did you see them abuse anybody?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see them do anything, but --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: You didn't see the police mistreat someone directly?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, thank you, those were my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness, you were somehow interrupted. You said, "I did not see them but -" and we could not hear "but what." Could you complete that sentence? Do you remember? That was three minutes ago or two.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were on the ground floor, and we were upstairs so what was going on, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: And you did not hear anything? You did not hear screaming or shouting or anything of that kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't see or hear well. I only saw and heard them taking people away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: And you did not hear accounts of what happened by such people when they came back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They weren't allowed to say much. They didn't dare to say much.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just another question. You were arrested on the 1st of August, 1993 and you were taken to the secondary school in Prozor. Do you know why you were arrested, what was the reason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't say why. They just rounded us up as civilians and took us off to that school. There were children and women there and elderly people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you were transferred from Prozor to the Heliodrom and when you arrived at the Heliodrom, were you asked to sign a piece of paper or were you taken to a cell without being registered? You remember being registered or not when you arrived in the Heliodrom? I'm not talking about the secondary school.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, sir, I think that this concludes your testimony. On behalf of the Judges I would like to thank you for testifying here, for assisting us in determining the truth. I wish you all the best and a safe return to your country and I will now ask the ushers to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Everything is fine now. Mr. Mundis, we'll continue and follow this marvelous procedure, at least as far as time is concerned. Mr. Mundis, the following witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. My colleague, Mr. Poryvaev will be taking the next witness who is ready to be brought into the courtroom. I turn over to my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, good afternoon, the next witness, while talking about the situation in the courtroom, sought some protection -- protective measures and that is pseudonym and face image distortion. The foundation: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll ask him to provide us with his reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will move into private session now. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are back in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness BM, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: My name is Vassily Poryvaev. I am counsel for the Prosecution and I will ask you some questions, first of all, relevant to the documents we have at our disposal and I intend to use as exhibits, and also I will clarify some positions in your witness statement. My first question: Do you remember being interviewed by someone from the International Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia from the Office of the Prosecutor? I mean the investigator.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. The former what? Could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: My question is: Were you ever interrogated, interviewed, by any investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor of the International Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia? That was my question.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: It's like this: I think it was in the year 2000 that I was contacted first by someone from the OTP, from The Hague, in Bugojno that was, and in Bugojno, during two days and then one day in Mostar, I gave statements, certain statements, which I wrote and signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like the usher to place the statement of Witness BM on the ELMO so that he could see the body of his statement. Our exhibit number of this statement: 09702.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Be careful because the name is on the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I suggest that this exhibit should be under seal for this very reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, do you see this document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Can you read it?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, this portion hasn't been translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Which portion?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, I can see. I apologise. I was looking at the wrong place. When I gave this statement, yes, that's fine, I performed the functions that it says there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, did you provide the investigator with a number of documents that were used as an attachment to your statement?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I would like to leaf through this exhibit so that the witness could take a look at the signatures and initials at the bottom of the body of the statement.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that instead of initials, you just did some extra work and just put your full signature?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I placed my full signature and how I sign my name, and as it says -- in the second row, that's how I sign my name on my ID card and my passport, where it just has the name for short.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, did you give your statement voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Completely voluntarily.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said his name so that should be redacted.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note they did not say the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I do not see his name in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters omitted the name.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He did say his name. He said I always sign my name that way and then he said his name. We all heard it. So I'm just telling the Court to take care because nothing will remain confidential if the name comes out.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that they heard the name but out of an abundance of caution did not say the name in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The name did not appear in the transcript whereas the witness recognises his name. Witness, the document in English that you signed has your name, bears your name, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, did you tell the truth to investigator?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I spoke the truth and it was my aim to say what I knew, and nothing but the truth, nothing but what I knew. Nobody influenced me in any way in giving any different kind of statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I would like to move the statement to the last page. I mean, its English version. Witness, do you see it?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. I see the 17th of February 2002. I see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Is it your signature?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is, the lower one, the bottom one. And up at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: But my signature is at the bottom as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Have you read your statement in your native language, after the interview?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I did. And unless I'm very much mistaken, the lady who wrote the statement down, I think, came from Tuzla. She was the interpreter, translator.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, now, do you recall your statement?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember all the details but everything that is written there and that I signed and initialed on each page of this statement I stand by.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much. As far as I understand --

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Because it was given over a period of three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, I would ask you to answer my questions and don't make too many comments because we are very limited in time. Were you given an opportunity of rereading your statement when you came here to the Tribunal for the meeting with the prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I had a copy with me before. I received a copy when I signed it. I was given a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Do you need to make some alterations or corrections in your witness statements now?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, it's like this: There are several places where there are possibly some mistakes, perhaps I said it wrong or somebody wrote it down wrongly, with some names and so on. So I remember seeing, for example, at one place, it says, "Simunovic Jozo" and it should be Simunovic Stipe" and maybe some other points. I didn't make a mistake with the surnames but there might have been two or three mistakes with the first names of the people concerned. Because there are quite a lot of names so I might have got them wrong, the first names, that is, but I knew -- know that with Simunovic Stipe, there is Jozo and there is Stipe so that's what led me to make that slip.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, we understand you. And perhaps this correction will be made in your witness statement in due time and in due course. The most important, that it is reflected now in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender this witness statement into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: While we are talking about this and correcting mistakes, on page 7 of the English version, two times in the second paragraph, and then again at the end of the fourth, the term "redrew" is used and I wonder whether it should not read "withdrew" or "withdrawing". Page 7, second paragraph, second line, "Zgela was redrewing a little." Shouldn't it be "withdrawing"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, would you take a look at the B/C/S version? What is the right word?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, while the witness is reading through the text, in future, it would be advisable that when you or your colleagues show the witness the statement during this procedure, you could say that we met yesterday and in my presence you read the testimony in your own language. Do you have any remarks to make today on that testimony or statement? Would you like to withdraw, correct something or not?" And he can say yes or no. And we can gain time that way because if we now go on to discuss words, individual words, whether it was redrawing or withdrawing or whatever, we are going to spend hours discussing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, at the session, proofing session, we had no such kind of statements from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: So, witness, what is the right word used by him?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: You mean paragraph 4? Towards the end of April 19 -- is that you mean, approximately at the end of April 1992? Could you repeat what you said, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, at approximately the end of April 1992, the position of Zgela was taken?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Zgela it should say, Josip Zgela. At the beginning he was the commander. Zgela, yes, Josip was his first name. It says "Zgelino" [phoen] here. No. Zgela is the right worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: "I was told that for the moment, he was redrawing a little because apparently," and so on and so forth. What was your term used in the witness statement?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: It says here he took over here, at the end of April, the position of Zgela was taken over by a Bosnian Croat named Andjelic from April to June of 1992 and very often there were replacements in HVO leadership in Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, please listen to me.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Zgela did not temporarily withdraw. Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Go on. "I was told" -- from this phrase. What was the word used by you, "redrawing" or "withdrawing"?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I apologise but in the -- is that the fourth paragraph that you're referring to on page 7? It says, "Approximately at the end of April 1992, the position of Zgela was taken over by a Bosnian Croat named, this is his surname, Andjelic, Andjelic is his surname, from the village of Podbor. He was born there but he didn't live there. So Zgela left and Andjelic came, Zgela was replaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Please, next sentence.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: "I was told that," this is what it says. It's like this. "He was replaced but I received information, that is to say, the gentleman was replaced by his -- by authorities so he left. He wasn't there any more."

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, just one word. Zgela was redrawing or withdrawing?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I was told that Zgela had withdrawn temporarily because the Bosnian Croats from Herzegovina did not like it when somebody from Croatia was in command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: It's quite clear now. Let's go on. So, Your Honour, I would like to tender this Exhibit 9702.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Murphy?

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to the admission of this exhibit, and I think we are still in private session, but -- no? We are in open session? All right. I don't think there is any need to go into private session. Your Honours, as I understand it this statement is being tendered under Rule 89(F). That rule does not give the Prosecution an absolute right to present any kind of evidence in written form, but only where the interests of justice allow. If we look at the content of this statement, if I could direct Your Honours to a number of passages in the English version, the -- at the beginning of page 4, the witness makes a statement dealing with an allegation about the crisis committee working directly under the orders of Zagreb and what he describes as its field office Grude. At the bottom of that same page, there are -- there is a mention of the media in the municipality being under the control of the HVO. On the next page, Your Honour, page 5 of the English version, in the fourth paragraph, the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I understand your objections, Mr. Murphy, but when you come to the cross-examination, you'll be able to put that to the Court and then you can make your conclusions and say that you are against having the document admitted, but you can do that during the cross-examination because you are intervening now at the moment when the Prosecutor is asking the witness whether he recognises what he already stated in written form. We are just starting out. So as to the substance of the document, you can challenge any points you like during the cross-examination, and then say that you challenge the admittance of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand Your Honour's point. I would like, however, to put this submission on the record because it seems to me that this is not an appropriate use of Rule 89(F) when a witness makes such far-reaching statements which go to the very heart of the joint criminal enterprise allegations in this case, it's appropriate for the Trial Chamber to hear an examination-in-chief so that the Judges can begin to observe the demeanour of the witness and to assess his credibility. Moreover, Your Honour, later in the statement, and I won't go into detail, to take up time, but Your Honours will have observed that there is a very, very long, well, a long passage dealing with the acts and conduct of one of the accused, which clearly would not have been admissible under 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, fine. You're quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're quite right but you know that several days ago, the Judges adopted a new article, 92 ter, providing for this procedure, with the possibility of having written statements relating to the conduct of the accused and their acts. So under 89(F), the old rule, that might have existed but now we are in a situation where we have 89(F) and 92 ter. But the objective is to try and proceed as quickly as possible and to give you as much time as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness has just told us that he stated several names incorrectly in his statement, and the Prosecutor tells us that we will have a correction in due course. I think these corrections would be very welcome immediately because those names are vital, as far as we are concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, quite. Thank you. Witness, you said that there were three surnames that you gave but you might have been wrong about the first names and you gave us one example. Do you have any other examples to give us that you would like to correct straight away? If that doesn't come to mind immediately, what you could do later on, during the break, because we are going to take another break, so when we take our break, you can read through your text, your statement, and then tell us which first and last names need to be corrected. That way, we'll save time. But move on to the documents, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, first I would like to call attention of the witness to pages 12 -- 11, 12 of the statement in English and page 12 in B/C/S, which commence with the words, "On the 14th of November." This is the last passage in the English version at the bottom. In the B/C/S version, it's the sixth passage from the top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps in order to save time, read out the beginning of that passage to him, that will help him find his bearings.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found it. It says, "On the 14th of November, 1992, an information report was written to inform President Alija Izetbegovic and the staff of the supreme headquarters in Sarajevo about the happenings in Prozor on the 23rd and 24th of October, 1992."

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, by whom was that report drafted and signed? I mean first of all, the organisation or body and then maybe some personalities.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: In the penultimate passage, it says that the drafters of this passage, prominent members of Prozor, were -- well, you have the names there and I'm included.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. But is it correct as reflected in your witness statement?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: These are the correct names. These are the people who drafted this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Now I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 744. You may take away the witness statement now for the moment and put it aside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may intervene before we have an answer, I'd like to follow up on my colleague Murphy's objection. You reminded us of the amendment to the rules. You mentioned Rule 92. However, may I draw your attention to the fact that these rules enter into force seven days after the date on which the official document is issued and that was the 22nd of September, 2006.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But that's why we are dealing with 89(F) but there is the spirit of the matter and the rules, the letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Perhaps there might be a better time to more fully address these types of legal issues but at this point, the Prosecution position is that the Defence teams will have adequate opportunity to cross-examine the witnesses pursuant to the Trial Chamber's guidance and time limits or time allowed by the Trial Chamber. The whole purpose of this exercise, as Your Honour has rightly indicated, is a time-saving device. The fact that the witness is present in court, that his credibility can be tested, that his demeanour can be observed, all of these things still exist under this procedure that we are using here today and so the fact of the matter is that Rule 89(F) is simply a means of expediting testimony. Rule 89(F), of course, this entire procedure is silent as to acts and conduct of the accused or any of a number of other issues. The fact of the platter is the witness is here, he's available for cross-examination, he's available to answer any questions that Your Honours may have, Your Honours may observe his demeanour and his credibility may be tested by anyone in this courtroom who so desires to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Mundis. The Prosecution may continue, and could the interpreters please interpret? Because I can't hear them right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: So, Witness, do you see a document on the screen?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I see the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I would like to scroll to the second page, scroll down. Witness, is this the document you meant in your witness statement when talking about the report dated on the 14th of November?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I can see part of the document here. I'm familiar with the contents of this report, and at the time that this report was drafted, I believe it reflected the situation such as it was at the time. It reflects the facts. This entire report reflects the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would like to take a look at page 1 in the English version, and page 1, passages 3, 4, in B/C/S. The next page in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The objective of this procedure is to advance rapidly. If you now start putting questions to him about the contents of the document, I don't see how we'll be saving time. If he can recognise the document, and says that that's the document in question, that's sufficient. It's not necessary to tell him, have a look at page 3 and tell me what is written down there corresponds to the situation you are familiar with, because this document, he obviously knows about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour. I withdraw my question. I'm quite happy with the response given by the witness before. Now I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 09694. [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Do you see the name of the body on behalf of which the document was drafted?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: It says the Party of Democratic Action, Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Did you participate in the drafting of this document?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, partially, but I am familiar with the document, and I accept it as my own, as if I had fully participated in its drafting, and I'm in total agreement with the contents of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would like now to turn to Exhibit 01656. Witness, do you remember giving this document to the investigator?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity of reading this document now, while being here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I have the document on me. I've always had it on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, do you confirm the contents of the document now?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Now I would like to turn to Exhibit 01542. It's not on the screen yet, I suggest.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have it, the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, do you remember this document?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I do and I stand by what the document states.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I would like to turn to Exhibit 00657. Witness, do you see this document?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, although it's not really legible but I am familiar with its contents and I stand by this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, Witness, just one question, just relevant to your statement: At some point you participated in some investigation of the events in Prozor municipality on the 23rd of October; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: How did you obtain your information which was then added in the documents which were submitted to the higher authorities of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: We had statements from eye-witnesses of the events, and we had information from people who were damaged, so we had interviews from witnesses, with witnesses, eye witnesses, and statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, did you receive any information from other sources, I mean your subordinates?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: After the events in Prozor, after the 23rd of October, for a few days, the situation was chaotic. There was information, there was misinformation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I'm sorry, just my question was quite precise. Did you get information from your subordinates for drafting these documents?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I would like witness to be shown Exhibit 09376. Have you ever seen this document?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I have, and I have it with me, not here but I do possess that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Do you confirm that the information in the document is accurate?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I can confirm that. It wasn't difficult to check this at a certain point in time. Don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Next, Exhibit 09429. Witness, do you see this document?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. And the contents of this document are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I would like to turn to Exhibit 09482. Yes. Witness, do you see this document?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, but this is just part of what subsequently happened in this village, because not a single house remained undamaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, and I have this document. At the time the contents of the document were correct and later the situation changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, thank you very much. I would like to turn to Exhibit 09482.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There must be an error in the transcript. It's not 09402 because this document has already been dealt with. It must be 09487, I assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, because of this rostrum, I don't see properly the screen. But you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I would like to turn to Exhibit 09487. Witness, do you see this document?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I stand by the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Next document [Microphone not activated]?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Next document 00640. Witness, do you see this document?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, the list isn't complete, there are 110 vehicles in total in this list and at the time that this document was drafted, it correctly reflected the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Next exhibit, 02180.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There must be a minor error because the document refers to 169 vehicles and the witness said 110 because he apparently didn't turn the page. As I don't miss anything --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's possible. I didn't turn the page over. You can't see it here. But there is one document that refers to 110 vehicles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Now I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 01188.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, do you see this document? (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Do you stand by it now?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Next exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I? I would like to ask a small question with regard to this document. You speak on the third line in the English translation, of course, of "mercenary hordes." Could you specify what you had in mind with this term?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When entering Prozor, the HV and HVO forces in October 1992, there was looting of the -- of Bosniak property in Prozor, all-out looting of their property. Over 90 per cent of the inhabitants of Prozor left Prozor in two days, they fled for Jablanica, Konjic and to the eastern part of the municipality of Prozor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: What I'm referring to in the B/C/S, I will try to pronounce it correctly, is, "B/C/S spoken" on the third line. What do you refer to? Who is that? "B/C/S spoken."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time when the document was drafted, according to the statements of expelled Bosniaks from Prozor, there were individuals who advanced and scared the population. They said those who are coming behind us, all they do is slaughter and kill and beat the people fleeing. They were just trying to save their lives. Everything that was of any value in Prozor was looted. Everything that belonged to the Bosniaks. And acts committed are referred to here in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This question could have been put in the course of the cross-examination or when the Judges put questions, but you didn't answer my colleague's question.
