My colleague has pointed out that it says that after the aggression in Gornji Vakuf, there were HVO units that participated with special units from the Republic of Croatia and with mercenary hordes. So we, the Judges, are interested in this naturally. What did you mean when we read this sentence, it seems that there are HVO units, there are specialist units, from Croatia, and there are mercenary hordes. There are three groups concerned. That's what it says in English. What can you tell us about this? Because you spoke about consequences. What we are interested in are the authors, the perpetrators, not the consequences.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my opinion, at the time when I drafted this, and on the basis of the information I had on what had happened in Prozor, the only proper way of describing the looting of that property was to say that someone came after the army, they took what they could take.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In the course of the cross-examination, we'll be able to come back to this subject. Let's move on. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go into private session before I say what I have to say, just very briefly, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the document? It's not on the screen yet, I'm sorry. 01425. I repeat the number of exhibit. Do you see it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Do you recognise the document?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Do you stand by it now?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I stand by what is written. I accept that what is written here is in good order.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: What do you mean by "good order"?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I accept that the content of the document at that time was a reflection of the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That was my final question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, for the sake of the transcript I'd like to point out that line 18 of this document, in line 18 reference is made to a previous document, and it concerns mercenary hordes. In line 18 it says that HVO forces include a mercenary group and soldiers from Croatia. During the course of the cross-examination, we can come back to this. The Prosecution has now finished with the presentation of their documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In future, Mr. Mundis, we could perhaps improve the procedure if we provided the witness with the bundle of documents and then the witness could go through the pages and, as you are speaking, he'll say yes, I recognise document 413, I recognise document 460, et cetera, because as you can see, now we have to wait for the document to appear on the screen so that the witness can have a look at it. As the Judges and Defence have the documents, we could save time in this way. So you could show these documents to the witness in this way and it would be faster. It's a suggestion I'm making but I think it's a good suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you for that guidance, Mr. President, just so as to avoid any confusion, my understanding of what you've just suggested is that we simply provide the witness with a bundle, a hard copy bundle of the exhibits and then we expeditiously take the witness through them. Is that -- we will certainly endeavour to do that, Mr. President. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's in the interests of everyone. It would make it possible to have a very efficient cross- examination then and to save time. If I remember things correctly, we said that the Prosecution would have two and a half hours, if I'm not mistaken, or, rather, the Defence will have two and a half hours because Mr. Mundis you had initially planned for two and a half hours of examination; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Mr. President, that was again before we had -- we were a bit squeezed for time to finish all the witnesses and before we decided to proceed with the 89(F) procedure with respect to this witness so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Defence, you have two and a half hours. Use it as you see fit. I don't know who will be starting. Perhaps you don't have any questions, in which case the Judges will put their questions. Mr. Ibrisimovic

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next Defence team, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have agreed with General Praljak's Defence to take the floor last. Thank you to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. That means it's my turn now but I do wish to say before I start that we have not yet agreed on the distribution of time among ourselves, but I will be free to put my questions until the break and then after the break we will inform Your Honours as to whether I can continue or whether the next team will start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Two and a half hours, that's 150 minutes and that means 25 minutes for each Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, excuse me, colleague Nozica, you said that General Praljak's Defence had a right to 50 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's quite right. We believed that General Praljak's Defence had the right to 50 minutes so that was the exception, so Ms. Nozica, you should have 25 minutes unless Mr. Pusic has given you his 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will proceed until the break and then I will agree with my colleagues. I am in a little bit of a dilemma that I wish to clarify. I think I heard the Prosecutor say that he asked that this witness's statement be under seal. This would greatly complicate my cross-examination because the aim of my cross- examination is to point out parts of the statement and to have it in e- court, which is the only way to deal with certain issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, if any passages might reveal the witness's identity, in that case, you should ask for us to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I have the statement in Croatian and there are no signatures on the pages so I think that is how it will appear in e-court. I don't believe there will be any problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Good day, sir, my name is Senka Nozica, and I will be examining you on behalf of Mr. Stojic's Defence. Just a little while ago you were shown a document so I would like to start there, it's a P 001188. We don't have to have it in e-court. It's about the mercenary hordes you mentioned in that document. It's a document you signed. Could you tell me, please, where you were on the 23rd of October 1992? Were you in Prozor?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. We will come to that. So what you write about in this letter, you heard from somebody else and then you described this?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I heard it from citizens of Prozor who had fled to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I am assuming that we came back to the same mistake again, revealing the witness's identity.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise but each one of my questions could reveal the identity of the witness. If the Prosecutor believes that I'm revealing the witness's identity by quoting from these documents, then this is bound to happen. It's very difficult for me to deal with this and I appeal to the Chamber to issue a decision. How else can I cross-examine if I am not to draw attention to parts of the statement where the witness explains where and when he was? I didn't mention any names, just event. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said that you heard about these events second-hand, on the 23rd of October, 1992, you say you were not in Prozor?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: It was a Friday.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, I wish to point to a part of your statement, it's on page 3 in Croatian. Could we please have it on e-court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which page in the English version?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the same page, number 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please, I will tell you slowly, you say that in mid-1991, the Bosnian Croats from Prozor started arming themselves. You also say that in mid-1991, a Muslim Crisis Staff was established. You say that both events took place in mid-1991.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Both events, first the Crisis Staff of the Croatian people was established, and a month or two later, in response, the Crisis Staff of the Bosniak people was also established. I think this was in September, after the arrival of Serbian and Montenegrin forces in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So in your statement, on page 3, you said erroneously that in mid-1991, the Crisis Staff of the Muslim people was established. Now you say it was in November?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I didn't say November. I said September, around September. Let me tell you, in the beginning, when this Crisis Staff was established, I was not a member of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you then tell us when this was? Because September is not mid-1991. Can you tell us whether you have this information or not? You can say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know the precise date for certain. I know it was established in 1991 and that the Crisis Staff of the Croatian people was established before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When was it established?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Because I was working in a school at that time, I was a teacher, I wasn't very interested until September in what was happening in Prozor, until the forces arrived and Prozor was under threat, because Serbian and Montenegrin forces arrived in Mostar. I think it was around the 18th of September but it may have been a few days before or after.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Does that mean that you don't actually know when it was established?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know precisely. It was in 1991. It was by the end of the third part of 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... have to intervene here. Is the question you're asking really important, is it really important on what exact date the Crisis Staff, Croatian Crisis Staff, was formed and then the Bosnian one or are you asking the question in order to see whether what he wrote and what he says is precise? Because the sentence says, "Mid-1991". So mid-1991 that could be July, August, September, give or take a month here or there. So it is it really important for your case or do you want to know whether the witness is saying things precisely? That's what I'd like to know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness spoke about many things, in the view of the Defence, approximatively, especially as regards dates and times. I believe that we have to establish logically what is correct because in his statement the witness provides precise dates. Some dates which are important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now, Witness, do you know exactly when the Croatian Crisis Staff was established or are you speaking in approximate terms? Can you give us a month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know precisely, but I do know it was in the first semester of 1991, by the end of the first semester. That means that the Croatian Crisis Staff was established before. I heard that from what people said. It was a small town. Everybody knew what was going on in the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I will only ask you not to start your answer before I finish because I have to switch my microphone on and off when I start and when I finish. This cannot be done if you start replying before I finish putting my question. On page 5 of your statement, it's also page 5 in English, in paragraph 2, you speak about an agreement between Milosevic and Tudjman. At the time, when these events were taking place, in 1991 and 1992, what did you know about this agreement?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I learned about it from the media, like all other citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It was widely reported in the newspapers and on television. I know it was frequently a topic in the media at the time. They said there had been secret talks. I didn't take part in them. I wasn't there. But it said that the division of Bosnia and Herzegovina had been discussed, and people said -- in Karadjordjevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you please answer more briefly? I don't want to interrupt you but please make your responses brief. On the same page, just a paragraph above that, you spoke about so-called observation units and you said that the Croats took their positions against the Serbs and that the Bosniaks did not participate in this. And now you say it was also evident that the Bosniaks of Bosnia-Herzegovina did not want war but a peaceful solution. Later on, we assisted the HVO in manning the observation points. Does that mean that in Prozor, the Bosniaks did not want war with the Serbs who had taken up positions overlooking Prozor? Is that what you meant to say?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I meant to say that on the basis of information and instructions coming from the then state leadership and Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, he kept saying, "We are not in favour of war. We want a peaceful solution. We have to do everything possible to find a peaceful solution." But as we know, this was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When we link this up with the agreement between Milosevic and Tudjman, you're a politician, I hear you held important positions in your party, was it logical for Milosevic and Tudjman to agree on a division of Bosnia? Why then would the Croats be manning a line facing the Serbs? Why would they have to do that if they had agreed?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: According to what I know and I'm not saying I'm right, I'm just telling you what I know, the practical implementation did not coincide with the interests of the parties because according to what the people were saying and what the media were saying, the division of Bosnia should have roughly been down the river Bosna and Neretva, western Croatia and eastern Serbia. However, Milosevic claimed something quite different. He wanted to claim everything where the Serbs lived, from Macedonia to Karlovag [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So they did not reach an agreement and an agreement -- you can only talk about an agreement if both sides agree?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, Madam, I think you know this better than I do, but they might have agreed but they didn't put that agreement into practice. They didn't implement it so it all fell through.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you tell us what option in March and April 1992 the Bosnian Croats favoured, March/April, 1992 is the year?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: All I can do is speak about the Prozor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Tell me, then. But previously, please.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, briefly. At the referendum, at the beginning of the first - - I think it was the 1st of March, 1993, a referendum was held. The Croats went to the elections together with the Bosniaks supported Bosnia- Herzegovina. They voted for it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So the Croats were in favour of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. They went to the elections and they voted for Bosnia- Herzegovina, in favour of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which means that on the territory of the state, about two-thirds of the overall population of Bosnia-Herzegovina voted in favour of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. That's what you say in your statement, and it is to be found on page 5. You say in March, April, of 1992 the Bosnian Croats and the Bosnian Muslims wanted an independent Bosnia-Herzegovina. The Bosnian Serbs did not want that. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I want to ask you something now about something that we started out from, our starting point, and that was the establishment of the HVO. And my first questions to you, the Crisis Staffs and the TO, and I'm referring to page 6 of your statement, page 6 of your statement, I think it coincides in the English version, it's also on page 6. You say sometime in March 1992 or the end of March 1992, the Bosnian Croats in Prozor municipality established the HVO. HVO was divided into two parts, the civilian and military part. Can you remember whether that was in March and how do you happen to remember that? Did you hear that about -- from someone? Where did you get this date March 1992 or were there rumours going around or what?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, already in March 1992, some units were formed of the Croatian Defence Council in Prozor, and that is why I said that and think that. But then I read some documents later on, and so I might be wrong on the exact day because I happened to read somewhere that Herceg-Bosna or rather the Croatian Defence Council was established in the -- on the 8th of April, 1992, around the 8th of April, I believe, and that there is a document which I looked through -- well, I'll tell you where I saw the document, a copy of the document, in fact. It was in a book written by Mr. Mesud Hero, and he has a copy of the decision on the establishment of the HVO included in the book, so maybe the decision was taken earlier but it was official then.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. You give us the wrong fact in your statement. You gave us the wrong fact in your statement. But you didn't have to read those books because you have the exact facts in your information of the 12th of March 1993 and it is Exhibit presented here from the information you signed on the 12th of March, 1993, and in that report or information note on page 2 of the Croatian version -- on page 3, I apologise, it's on page 3 in the Croatian version, you state the following: You say that the HVO was established on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps the counsel gives the number of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's what I was going to ask counsel. What is the exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll give the exhibit number right away. But I don't want to open the document because it will take too much time. I think it is P 016 -- P 01656. It is page 2 in the Croatian version and page 4 in the English. And the date mentioned there is the 10th of April. Now, the witness has said the 8th of April, 1992, whereas the date mentioned in the document is the 10th of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So if we say that it was in April and correct your statement on that score, do you say that at the end of March 1992, the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina ordered that every municipality had to establish a Territorial Defence, TO? Was that so?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Now, can you tell me whether Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time was recognised by the international community, had been recognised as a state by the international community because we are still in the end of March 199 -- at the end of March 1992, when we mentioned the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about Bosnia-Herzegovina. I don't know the exact date whether it was recognised by the United Nations but as the population went out to vote in a referendum, that was enough, as far as I was concerned, and it is true that the then Presidency ordered that TO Defence Staffs were established in all the municipalities where they had been abolished and the deadline was from the 1st to the 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You're not a lawyer, so those dates are not important for you but I think that dates are important for the Court. You said you didn't know. Now, this Territorial Defence, was it the Territorial Defence which was in favour of the -- or rather, it took away all the weapons from you in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I said that the Presidency made the decision to establish Territorial Defence staffs where they had not existed -- where they weren't in existence and in Prozor it had been disbanded, the former Territorial Defence Staff had been disbanded, abolished.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Why had it been abolished or disbanded?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know why, but I do know that it was in 1991, but don't hold me to that. Perhaps I might be wrong on the date. Any way, that the former -- a former member of the Presidency of Yugoslavia, Mr. Raif Dizdarvic, I think it was Raif Dizdarvic, I it was one of them but I think it was Raif Dizdarevic in actual fact, that he ordered that all weapons be come confiscated from the Territorial Defence and that they should withdraw to the military barracks so as to avoid conflicts and that was the wrong move to make.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. It was the wrong move to make. You're quite right on that score. Now, tell me, please, when was the TO in Prozor established?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: On the 1st of April, 1992 (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, but could the usher hand round these documents? So may I have the usher's help, please? I think this is the time to distribute these copies of the document. We have three for Their Honours and one for the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps in -- on page 68, line 9, we should redact. Now we are dealing with the position to which the witness was appointed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Very well. Mr. Registrar, redact that, please. Counsel Nozica, continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said the 1st of April. Might that not have been the 28th of March?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No, because on the 1st of April I was appointed and the Crisis Staff of the Bosniak people sent in a request to the district staff of Zenica to do that and I was officially appointed on the 1st of April but the Crisis Staff at its meeting held several days prior to that, two or three days before, sent in that request, but my letter of appointment says the 1st of April, 1992, which is when the official Territorial Defence Staff was established in Prozor and it was incomplete to begin with. Didn't come up to strength.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Perhaps it was the other way around.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No, because the previous Territorial Defence had been disbanded in 1991. I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we take a look at the document then? I think this would be important. It is document P 01656. I don't want to go into too great a detail but I think it says something different because you're being very categorical. It is on page 3 in Croatian and page 4 in the English. Page 4 in the English. I'll read it out. Or perhaps you can read it for yourself. I just want to make sure where it is in English. It is in the last paragraph, the middle of the last paragraph on the right-hand side. You can see the date, the 28th of March. From the unexplainable positions of some of the members in Prozor, at meetings with the HDZ of Prozor, and on those occasions, labels were hurled at one another. The TO was formed on the 28th of March 1992, with the participation of the representative of the SDA and the Crisis Staff of the Muslim people, and this Crisis Staff of the Muslim people was allegedly established at the beginning of February 1992. So that brings us to the date when you claimed was the formation of the Muslim Crisis Staff. You said September 1992. Whereas here it says February 1992. And the TO was formed on the 28th of March, 1992, and not the 1st of April, as you claim. So this is an information that you signed. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Madam, I don't think you understood me. What I said was this: The Crisis Staff made a decision to establish a Territorial Defence Staff, but for it to take effect, the ultimate decision must be taken by the district staff of Zenica. (redacted) (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. I understood you now and I understood you a moment ago the first time when you said that the Crisis Staff of the Muslim people was established in September whereas here you say February, which means before the Croatian people set up their Crisis Staff. And you said that the TO staff was established in April, and you're signing it on the 28th of March. This is your report.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: This was written on the 17th of February, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Then tell us that you didn't say the right thing in your statement but what you wrote in the information was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Again we should make a redaction because the position was revealed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Mr. Registrar, would you issue an order to that effect? Counsel, Nozica we are spending a great deal of time between the 28th of March and the 1st of April, only three days before. I don't see where this is leading. Why you're investing such a lot of energy in to defining this three days.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is seven months difference from the time that the witness said he -- the Crisis Staff, Muslim Crisis Staff, was established and what it says in the information and I'll say why I'm raising that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: From these facts and figures, sir, we can conclude that the Crisis Staff of the Bosniak people was established before the Croatian Crisis Staff, can we?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I can't confirm that but what I know is this --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: May we continue? Can I move on? Can you confirm that the TO of Prozor municipality composed of the Bosniak people was formed before the HVO?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Units were formed in the municipality, but organised units of the HVO existed in Prozor before the municipal staff in Prozor. They were formed. Now, who took the decision about their formation prior to -- previously, I don't know. It wasn't an important point and I didn't check it out. I didn't check out when it was. But units on the ground did exist before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, you worked in this field for a long time. I don't want to have to redact the transcript but you worked for a long time in all these structures. Now, those units, could they have existed before they were officially formed? So were there some non-official, illegal units? Because could the TO have existed before it was established?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No. The TO could not have existed before it was officially established.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But you're saying that the HVO could.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No. I said that there were organised forces of the HVO on the territory of the municipality before the establishment of the Territorial Defence forces in Prozor and that's the truth 100 per cent, yes, they did exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel, we are spending a great deal of time on this. I have to channel the cross-examination in order to avoid wasting time. The witness has on several occasions asserted that the HVO in Prozor was constituted before the Territorial Defence of the Bosniak people. If you have any proof to the contrary, put it to the witness. Show him. And then we'll have things clear. Because you keep asking your question and he keeps answering the same thing. Now, if you have something to put to the witness, which refutes what he has said, pursuant to Rule 90 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, show him that he's wrong. Perhaps you have some orders, documents, which prove that the Bosniak Territorial Defence existed before the HVO. If you have anything like that, put them to the witness, show him the documents. Otherwise, move on, because he is constant in maintaining his position. HVO units, he says, were established before the Territorial Defence of the Bosniak people.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems that I'm doing my job very badly, Your Honour, because if it is not evident from what I have put to the witness, then I don't know. I put it to the witness and the witness said that the HVO was formed first and then the Territorial Defence. The witness also said that the HVO was officially established on the 8th of April 1992. And that he learned that later on (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, we should make a correction, redaction. I mean, on page 73, 14. Line 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, let's have a redaction. We have to have a break now because we've been working for more than an hour and a half, for technical reasons, I've been informed by the registrar that we need to have a half an hour break. So we'll be resuming at 6.10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will resume now.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement, on page 9, of the Croatian version, at the very bottom of the page, and it's page 9, paragraph 4 in the English version, you refer to an incident that took place on the 23rd of October 1992 at a meeting, and you said that on that occasion, after a short dispute, Ilija Petrovic returned and said while they are sitting over there and drinking coffee the Territorial Defence was killing members of the HVO in the east, and this concerned the incident on which occasion the Territorial Defence from Gornji Vakuf killed a HVO member. His name was -- the name of that member was Zadro from the village of Dobrosa; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could we have 2D 00054 on the screen? It's from the registry of the dead for Zadro and since it states that he is from Dobrosa, from Prozor Rama, you can have a look at it, his name is Franjo. The date of his death is the 23rd of October, 1992, 1300 hours. Is that the person you had in mind in your statement?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. And you continue to say in your statement, this was now used by the HVO in Prozor as an excuse to leave the meeting. But first of all I'd like to ask you whether you know whether, in some of your statements there was a dilemma as to whether anyone had been killed in fact, and did you state in some statement that certain things were checked and that no members of the Croatian army were killed on that day?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Madam, when I was in Idovac with part of the army and when I withdrew from there, when I arrived at Makljen, when I passed through with 30 soldiers, the body of that soldier was still there, and members of the Gornji Vakuf Brigade told me that he had been killed on the 22nd. I'm not claiming that he was killed on that date but they told me he was killed on the 22nd and he was still there on the ground, his dead body was still there. I saw him there on the 24th. He was dead at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could we see P 01656? It's a report dated the 12th of March, 1993. Could we have a look at page 9 in the Croatian version, the first paragraph, and page 10, the first paragraph, in the English version? This is a report, you know what it's about?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It's a report from the year 1993, and you signed it too?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And in the report, you say the following: On that occasion all the army members, all the members of the Croatian delegation, left the premises where negotiations were taking place. There was a radio link from the staff of the army, BH Prozor, and they confirmed that there was no killing at that time in that area. At 1525, there was an intensive artillery attack and you said that you saw that body in October.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Just a minute. We mustn't overlap. On the 10th of March 1993, in the -- in report, you say that the information was checked and no one had been killed. How can you explain this difference?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, the member referred to wasn't killed in territory of the municipality of Prozor. He was killed in part of Makljen, in the northern part of Makljen. It's called Crni Vrh. That's where he was killed. He was killed by members of the ABiH from Gornji Vakuf, so he wasn't killed in our area. That's for sure. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: How do you know? Was an investigation launched into his killing? Did they determine who killed him and where?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No, as far as I know, no one on our side conducted an investigation but I saw the body, the body was on the ground, and they didn't touch him for a few days. I don't know when they took him away. I saw him lying on the ground, a member of the Territorial Defence from Gornji Vakuf shot him, one of them told me who was there in the unit that they had killed a HVO member from Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You say that no one conducted an investigation after that?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I'm not claiming that but I don't know. On our side, no one conducted an investigation because this incident didn't take place in the area under the control of the ABiH in the municipality of Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'll leave Mr. Praljak's Defence the possibility of determining which area you were located in at the time but let's continue with this statement of yours. You say that the negotiations were interrupted, the HVO left the meeting and 15 minutes later, there was an attack on Prozor, so that was on the 23rd of October, 1992 at 1530. Does the name Asim Hadzovic mean anything to you, a member of the 4th Corps of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: At that time, the 4th Corps didn't even exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We are talking about the 7th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, 7th of December, that's fine, but I don't know that man.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the ABiH 4th Corps at the time?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: The commander of the ABiH 4th Corps was Mr. Arif Pasalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Does the name Mirsad Catic mean anything for you?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Mirsad Catic, I've heard that name somewhere but I don't know in what context. Perhaps his nickname is Cuperak.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: At the time, was Mirsad Catic the commander of the municipal staff?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Where? In Prozor?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: What date?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: On the 7th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could we have a look at the following document?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Let me just add something. Towards the end of October, 1992, after the fall of Prozor, someone was temporarily appointed as commander of the staff from Prozor or Konjic. His name was Mirsad Cukle but he only had that position a few days. He's still alive today.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could we have a look at Defence document 2D 00148, the first page in the Croatian version and it's also the first page in the English version. Could we just have the Croatian version? I don't know whether the witness can read this.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: It's not very legible. Could you read it out for me perhaps because it's difficult for me. Now it's better.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. We can see the name Asim Hadzovic, a member of the ABiH 4th Corps, 7th of December. He is submitting a written report on disciplinary investigations conducted. There is a decision dated the 3rd of December, 1992. A commission was formed. Have you ever heard about this commission that consisted of Asim Hadzovic, Kemal Jusufovic and Mustafa Begovic. It had to do with disciplinary proceedings.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I've never seen this document. I can't confirm its authenticity.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm not asking you to do that. But do you know these people I've mentioned?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Zejnil Delalic whom you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know that disciplinary proceedings were instituted against Mr. Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Zejnil Delalic was based in Konjic and I was based in Stipe. In the territory of Prozor municipality, I only had a radio post. I didn't have any other means of communication and it wasn't necessary for me to communicate with Mr. Zejnil Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could we have a look at the -- at page 2 in the Croatian version? It's the last paragraph that's been translated. The entire document hasn't been translated. It will be. But only what is stated in the last translated paragraph is of importance to this witness. I'll tell you what it's about now, and let's see if you can remember this. This commission was formed -- I'm going back to the first page so that I can read it out to you, and Delalic Amir was also a member. Let's have a look at the previous page in the Croatian version. It says that the commission from Mostar set off at about 11.00 and arrived in Parsovic about 1300 hours. We were received by the commander of the municipal staff there, Mr. Mirsad Catic, together with his associates and the commander of the Neretvica Brigade, Mr. -- full stop. Mr. Catic Mirsad, commander of the municipal staff briefly informed the commission of the situation and informed us of certain other elements and then certain other elements are mentioned. Certain other information that he had obtained in the investigation against Zejnil Delalic and the prison warden in Celebici, Zdravko. And on the second page, in the first, second and third paragraph it says, "Zejnil Delalic is guilty for everything that took place in the territory of the zone of his zone of responsibility." What was Mr. Zejnil Delalic's zone of responsibility in 1992 up until the month of December?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Zejnil Delalic, as far as I know, I haven't seen these documents but as far as I heard, at the beginning of August, I don't know the exact date, at the beginning of August 1992 he was appointed as the commander of the Igman operative group. At the command place Igman. And he didn't have command over the territory of Prozor municipality. It was only in August that he became commander of this group. Up until August he was a coordinator between the Territorial Defence Staff in Konjic and the municipal bodies of power. He was a coordinator.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could we have a look at document P 00413? And then we'll come back to Zejnil Delalic, given your answer. P 00413. We can see the date, the 8th of August, 1992. It's addressed to -- I apologise, the 28th of August, 1992. It's addressed to the municipal staff of the BH armed forces, order -- I haven't got much time but it's an order signed by Zejnil Delalic. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So in August, could he have any contact or any relation with Prozor and the municipal staff in Prozor?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No. In 1998, at this Tribunal, I was asked about this. I can claim with full responsibility that Zejnil Delalic couldn't have signed this. At that time, I told the Chamber that they should get a graphologist, a writing expert, to see whether Zejnil Delalic had signed this but even if he had signed this, this order wouldn't have been valid because Prozor municipality was not under his command.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about that. You've seen this document. You've seen that he has signed this.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. But you've seen that order and the Prosecution provided this order to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. You've said something important. This document provided by the Prosecution, P 413 is the number, the date is the 28th of August and it's signed by Delalic, commander of the Territorial Defence in Prozor. It's an order which, in view of an incident that took place on the 27th of August, not the 23rd, a request is made to withdraw the armed forces from Bosnia and Herzegovina under control -- under the control of the municipal staff, et cetera. And you say that this is a false order because at the time Delalic wasn't commander of the Prozor Territorial Defence. That's what you said a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. At this time, the commander on that day, the commander of the Territorial Defence of Prozor municipality was Muharem Sabic, Muharem Sabic, Muharem Sabic. And the day before the decision was issued I was at Idovac at the positions there when the incident at Prozor occurred. This was on Thursday, the 7th of August. You can check this. I know the precise date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as you're concerned, the document that you're being shown is one that you challenge; is that right? You're challenging the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was not the commander of the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence at the time. I'm 100 per cent sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: The Bench is always curious today. There is something that must be set straight. We are talking about an order dated 28th of August. You have told us, Witness, that the day before, you had -- you were at somewhere else, at the positions. This was, I read.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At Idovac, not in Prozor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You say this was Thursday the 7th of August. That would not be the day before. That would be three weeks before the 28th of August.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 27th of August, there was an incident when a group of HVO extremists arrived in Prozor and riddled some buildings with bullets. They caused great damage to buildings owned by Bosniaks and it was only due to the presence of mind of the then commander of the municipal staff that a tragedy was avoided and nobody was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You have now corrected the date and said 27th of August, while before you had said or it is in the record 7th of August and that means that this is settled.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was the 27th, the 27th. It was a Thursday. I even know the day. You can check and you'll find that the day was a Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I only wish to make a correction. The witness knows this very well. Mr. Zejnil Delalic at that time was not the commander of the TO staff. He was the commander of tactical group 1 and that is what it says here in this document. TG 1. Not TO. TG.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: TG, tactical group.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: After this, I wish to ask you did you know Zejnil Delalic's brother?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: His brother lived in Prozor. His name was Zahid. He was known as Zajka. He has died in the meantime. He lived and worked in Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: As you were very quick to describe these people as extremists, who attacked on the 27th as you say, could we take a look at document 2D 00055? 2D 00055. It's a report on the work of the Prozor municipal staff and it was signed by Mr. Muharem Sabic on the 16th of September 1992. Take a look at page 1, please. And then let's go back to page 2, in the English language, or, rather in the Croatian language, and page 2D 0600021 in English. I think that's also page 2. Let's see what Muharem Sabic says about these people you call extremists and everything you said. It's the first it -- fifth paragraph in Croatian. Relations with the HVO are not at a satisfactory level which was best seen in the night of August the 27th to 28th, 1992, when there was even a conflict in the town of Prozor in which there were wounded on both sides. Those who were in Prozor at the time say it was a conflict, but you, who were not in Prozor, say it was an attack by Croatian extremists. Who was closer to these events and who was in a better position to know what actually happened? You or Mr. Sabic? Mr. Sabic could know more details because he was a commander. [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: But let me tell you there was a document to show I'm right. A meeting was held after this and the Croats, the chief of the municipality, agreed to make good the damages done to the Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This does not prove there was an attack. It could have been a conflict between two sides as explained by Mr. Sabic. Can we go back to 2D 00148, page 2 in Croatian and I will conclude with this. This is the document we have just seen, a document of the 4th Corps, 2D 00148. I read out page 2 to you a while ago and the last paragraph which is translated into English, it's dated in December. The commander of the corps is reporting on disciplinary proceedings against Zejnil Delalic and it says the following: "With respect to Zejnil Delalic, it is mentioned that he's guilty of everything that took place in his area of responsibility. With respect to Colonel Jovan Divjak, he suspects that he was involved with Zejnil regarding the actions at Prozor and provoking a conflict between Muslims and Croats and that there was supposed to be a war on a wider territory so that the Muslims would be drawn into a war against the Croats. Also it was mentioned that Colonel Divjak was aware of Zejnil's order and that he did not take the necessary measures although he was present in the area." Can we show page 5 to the witness? Not to confirm authenticity but just so that the witness can see who the document was signed by. Thank you. There is a commission here, Asim Hadzovic, Kemal Jusufovic, Mustafa Begovic and Amir Belalovic [phoen]. Are you aware, sir, that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the 4th Corps conducted an investigation because there were grounds to suspect that the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina had provoked a conflict with the Croats in the area of Prozor?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I know that the 4th Corps conducted an investigation but I don't know who these people are. I know that as a consequence of that investigation, Mr. Jovan Divjak was detained in the primary school in Pasovici. I saw him there personally because at that time, I had known Jovo Divjak for 20 years. I know that at that time, when Mr. Divjak was detained, Mr. Zejnil Delalic fled from Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. That's all I wanted to know. Thank you. Thank you, Your Honours. I have completed my cross- examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We have exactly 25 minutes left for another Defence team -- 20 minutes. Yes, 20 minutes. Who is going to start off?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, excuse me, it's 20 minutes today but we have more in total.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Good day, sir, let me introduce myself. My name is Nika Pinter. I'm an attorney-at-law from Zagreb. I'm Defence counsel for General Praljak. Please let me finish my question and switch off my microphone and then begin speaking. Otherwise we will not get anything done. For the sake of one question can we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: When asked by my colleague, you spoke about Zejnil Delalic and the Konjic tactical group and you are familiar with that unit, are you not?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: TG Konjic?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I think they were officially called TG 1. I think it was a little different but it was called the tactical group 1, and it was the successor of another tactical group.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Very well. What matters is that you know what unit this was. In your statement, you say that on the 2nd of November, 1992, there was a meeting in Konjic which you were supposed to attend but your car broke down and you were late and then you waited in Konjic for Vehbija Karic and Zejnil Delalic to come back from Prozor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: You met them and they told you what had transpired at the meeting in Prozor and what decisions or agreement had been achieved there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown document 3D 00418? When the document shows up, would you please pay attention to the part of the text under point 5? I'll ask you whether -- well, we can't read the document yet. Can we please zoom in on point 5? It says here that at 1500 hours, a meeting was held in Prozor. Do you see the text here?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: It's not very legible.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Yes, true. I don't have a better version either. If we can zoom in a little bit. I will read and please try to follow. Well, now we can see it. You can see that at 1500 hours a meeting was held and the attendees are listed. You know Vehbija Karic, you also mentioned Arif Pasalic.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: He was the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: With his escort, then Safet Rucovic [phoen], Camil Skokovic, Zijad Demirovic and Zejnil Delalic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I was invited to the meeting. I was supposed to attend but I wasn't there as I said in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: This document says that these people were in Prozor and that they talked to General Praljak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Does it say in this document that as they were walking around Prozor, a renegade team of the HVO and HOS were roasting a lamb, they were dragging a flag with lilies through the mud and so on and so forth, but not even Praljak had the authority to make them listen to him. They were talking about Balijas, saying it was better for them not to come back, and they were making fun of and threatening us with BH army insignia. In this situation, no one could guarantee the safe return of the families who had fled or the soldiers of the army. There are still seven members detained and so on. Promising that on the next day they would be conditionally -- provisionally released. General Praljak was evidently embarrassed because of the situation and he issued several oral orders and was intending to issue a written order on the following day. Was that the situation Vehbija Karic and Delalic described on their return to Konjic?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, they didn't describe all the details but they said they had seen a very unpleasant situation. There wasn't enough time for them to tell me all the details but I was surprised by something that was allegedly and I stress allegedly Mr. Arif Pasalic, when he entered Prozor, at the fire station, it said the Ustasha centre or the Ustasha club. He said that on television. He said when he entered Prozor, he saw this written there and then someone present, possibly General Praljak, ordered that this be taken down. So there was certainly that inscription there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you. In connection with this document, I wish to ask you the following: In the document it says that General Praljak issued oral orders and promised to make them in writing. Is that correct? Is that what I have just read out?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. You have read this out.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: It states so here?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, but as I was not there, I cannot confirm it. I believe that if they wrote this down, then Mr. Praljak did it. I believe that. Whether it was implemented, I don't know. Well, that's open, an open issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please show the witness 3D 00290. [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: This meeting and the report, when it was, on the 4th of November, 1992; is that right? That's what it says. Now after the 4th of November, you have a document before you and the date on that next document is the 6th of November, 1992. It is an order. Now, if we were to go to the bottom of the order, the end of it, on page 2, you will see that the order was issued by General Major Slobodan Praljak, and there are two stamps. The department of Defence of Herceg-Bosna and the Territorial Defence, with the Territorial Defence insignia there. Can you see that? The left -- the stamp on the left. There are two stamps. You can see that there are two. One with the lilies. Can you see that? [Microphone not activated]?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Now, linked to this order --

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I can't see a lily there. No lilies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the left is the joint command of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO. On the left-hand side. You have half the coat of arms, which is the Bosnian, and half is the Croatian coat of arms.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: I think you can see that clearly.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Do you know about this order? Were you aware of it?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I do but it was never implemented.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: There were never any mixed controls?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And where were you?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Don't keep saying what you were.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I was -- I came to take up the post at the beginning of November with headquarters in Scipe.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So you weren't in the area where this order referred -- which this order refers to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop for a moment. Mr. Registrar, please have that redacted for the transcript. You didn't indicate it was 3D 000419. Was that the number of the document? You didn't say it, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 3D 00419. It's the same as 3D 00290. But 3D 00419 has the archive stamp so there is no doubt about its provenance. I should now like to have the witness answer the following question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: According to your statement you were arrested at the end of November 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Also pursuant to an order from General Praljak you were released the next day; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I have to say a few sentences to explain.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please, microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, because Mr. Praljak came from a meeting in Konjic with Mr. Begic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: We'll come to that. What I'm asking you now is whether you were released the very next day?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Were you interviewed or interrogated while you were incarcerated?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, interrogated and beaten.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: I'd like to show the witness another document now, it is P 889. Or perhaps it is 0889 because it is a Prosecution document, P 0889, 00889 is the document number. It is a criminal report filed against you. Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: No. Who filed it?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, the Croatian Defence Council the date is the 10th of December, 1992, in that criminal report among other things it is stated that it is filed against you. However, that -- a conversation with you was conducted and pursuant to Slobodan Praljak, General Major, you were released, that you went to the Konjic municipality where you most probably reside at present. May we take care that the witness's name does not appear? Because it's on the document. On the screen. But that corresponds to the time you were interrogated. That is to say the 29th of November 1992. Right?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: It is correct that I was arrested and interrogated then, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And you were released pursuant to an order from General Praljak?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, because Mr. Praljak came from Konjic, from a meeting where I was supposed to attend too at Zlatar. I wasn't there. They informed Mr. Praljak. They told him to go there. Mr. Praljak arrived together with Zlatko Velic and they released me and we decided on certain activities ad I was let go.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now apart from you, some other individuals were released when you were released?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Together with me, when I was arrested, there were 15 other soldiers from the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: May the witness now be shown the next document, it is 3D 00291. It is a report which is dated the 18th of December 1992, and it says that General Praljak arrived in Prozor and upon his arrival, immediately upon his arrival, he issued orders for the group of detainees to be released and amongst that group were you yourself. So that bears out what you said; right?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, the 30th.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Now, General Praljak will discuss what the meeting was about, which subjects were discussed. All I'm going to ask you now is something linked to the Territorial Defence. When you said that there was a decision to form units of the Territorial Defence -- or rather when did you say that happened?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I received an order for my appointment, the decision was prepared to -- by the Crisis Staff. But it was the district staff of Zenica that had the final say. In the order of the district staff of Zenica, it said that I was appointed to that duty, that I was appointed to, on the 1st of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: I didn't ask you when you were appointed. I asked you when the units of the Territorial Defence were established.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, this is how it was. The first official unit that the staff set up, the first official unit established, was established on the 3rd of April. (redacted) (redacted). I worked there before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: In answer to a question from Counsel Nozica, you referred to a decision by the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina by which units of the Territorial Defence are established, shall be established.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Madam, the order was to form Territorial Defence Staffs. Now the formation of -- it was the staffs that form units, that establish units.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: May the witness be shown the next document, 3D 000420? 3D 000420. Have we got that up on the screen? It is a decision, as you can see, by the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which says that on the 27th of May, 1992, units of the Territorial Defence be formed. Is that what it says? On the formation of Territorial Defence units?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Now, would you read out point 1? Which was the first territorial unit to be established?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: The following unit of the Territorial Defence is being formed, under number 1 it says the Bosnian Herzegovinian Brigade the Kraj Tomislav and as brigade commander, General Mate Sarlija is appointed. The TO Zenica Brigade, that was someone else. Et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: All right. Fine. So if you look at the names there, play we scroll down, please, to see the bottom of the document? Yes. If you look at those names, who were the commanders of the brigades or, rather, Territorial Defence detachments?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Ethnically speaking?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mate Sarlija was a Bosniak but he took the name of Mate Sarlija but he's not a Croat at all although he took that name. He's not a Croat. I can't remember but I will remember in due course his name was really Batlak.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Nijaz Batlak?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know about Nijaz but I know that he was Batlak. I'm quite certain of that and I met him on one occasion so he wasn't a Croat at all, he was a Muslim, a Bosniak, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Yes, we agree, sir.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, that's how it was. You needn't agree but that's how things were.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And the other names are Bosniaks, Muslims, right?

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I just happened to know number 5 on the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Look at the names.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I know Mr. Sehovic, I knew him. And as for the rest.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: That will do. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RAGIB MULAHUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know any of the others.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions. I'll leave sometime for the general. He has questions of his own which he can put tomorrow, I assume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, because it's already five minutes past 7.00. Theoretically speaking, General Praljak has, well, just do the maths, how much time, to see how much time he has. I think he should have around 30 minutes, unless I'm very much mistaken but the registrar will correct me if I'm wrong. As I said, it is five minutes past 7.00, I invite you all back tomorrow whether the proceedings reconvene at 2.15. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 21st day of September, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.04 p.m.,
